name: MonarchAiInlinePrompt
title: AiInlinePrompt
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchAiPromptInput, and androidx.compose.foundation.text.contextmenu.modifier.appendTextContextMenuComponents for the selection-menu item
summary: A prompt about selected text: an "Ask AI" action in the text selection menu that opens a bottom sheet with an excerpt of the selection, a prompt field and quick prompts.
whenToUse: In documents, emails or notes where AI rewrites what the person selected, opened from the selection menu or from a visible button such as "Edit paragraph with AI".
whenNotToUse: For an open-ended conversation, use MonarchAiPromptInput in an assistant screen. For suggesting the value of one form field, use MonarchAiAutofillField. For completing text as it is typed, use MonarchAiGhostText.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchAiInlinePrompt(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, onSubmit: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, context: String? = null, suggestions: List<String> = emptyList(), initialValue: String = "", closeOnSubmit: Boolean = true, pending: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels = MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels(), sendIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
@Composable public fun MonarchAiInlinePromptArea(onAskAi: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable public fun MonarchAiInlinePromptArea(state: TextFieldState, onAskAi: (selection: String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

public class MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, inputLabel: String? = null, submit: String? = null, context: String? = null, suggestions: String? = null, pending: String? = null)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called when the sheet should close: after a swipe down, a tap on the scrim, Back, or after sending with closeOnSubmit. Stop showing it.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the trimmed prompt or the tapped suggestion. Never called with blank text or while pending.

options.name: context
options.description: What the prompt acts on, usually the selected text. Shown as an excerpt of at most 140 characters under the label "Selection".

options.name: suggestions
options.description: Quick prompts such as "Shorten". Tapping one sends it at once.

options.name: initialValue
options.description: The text the field starts with each time the sheet is shown, with the caret after it.

options.name: closeOnSubmit
options.description: Slides the sheet away and calls onDismissRequest after sending. Off, the sheet stays and the field is cleared.

options.name: pending
options.description: A request is being sent: the field, Send and the suggestions are disabled and "Sending…" is shown and announced.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: label, placeholder, inputLabel, submit, context, suggestions, pending.

options.name: sendIcon
options.description: The Send button's icon. The button shows the word Send without it and is named Send either way.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea onAskAi
options.description: Wrap a SelectionContainer or a text field: "Ask AI" is added to its selection menu, and picking it closes the menu and calls onAskAi.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea state, onAskAi
options.description: The text-field overload: the item is added only while text is selected in state, and onAskAi receives the selected text.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea enabled
options.description: Off, the menu item is not added.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea label
options.description: The menu item's text; the built-in "Ask AI" without it.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea content
options.description: The selectable text or the text field, placed in a Box.

states.name: open
states.description: The sheet is fully expanded (no half-open stop), the prompt field has focus and the keyboard opens.

states.name: empty
states.description: Send is disabled until the field holds text other than spaces.

states.name: with context
states.description: An excerpt box with the AI border shows "Selection" and the first 140 characters of the context, cut with an ellipsis.

states.name: pending
states.description: The field, Send and the suggestions are disabled and "Sending…" appears under them.

states.name: closed
states.description: After sending (with closeOnSubmit), a swipe, a scrim tap or Back, onDismissRequest is called and the app stops showing it.

appearance: A Material 3 bottom sheet on the surface fill. The excerpt sits in a box with the subtle fill and the AI border role, its label in the strong AI color and the excerpt in muted text. The prompt box and the primary Send button come from MonarchAiPromptInput; suggestions are ghost buttons. Dark and both high-contrast themes swap the same roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a floating popover anchored to the selection rectangle. Android has no such floating panel for a selection; the platform pattern is an item in the system selection toolbar plus a bottom sheet, so this is two parts: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea for the toolbar item (a wrapper rather than a Modifier, because the built-in label is a string resource and the Foundation API that hands a Context to the menu builder is internal) and MonarchAiInlinePrompt for the sheet. There is no anchor, side or align, and no returnFocusTo: when the sheet's window closes the system gives focus back to the window underneath. The web's open and onOpenChange become the Material 3 idiom of showing the sheet while a state is true with onDismissRequest. The keyboard hint line of the web is left out, because touch is the main input; a hardware keyboard still sends with Enter, adds a line with Shift+Enter and closes with Escape (Back). With closeOnSubmit off the field is cleared after sending, where the web keeps the text. Compose does not expose the selected text of a SelectionContainer, so the app passes context itself; the TextFieldState overload reads the selection of a text field. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The sheet's content has the pane title "Ask AI", and the same text is shown as a heading.
The prompt field takes focus when the sheet opens and is named "Prompt".
The excerpt is one TalkBack element that reads "Selection" followed by the excerpt.
The quick prompts are a traversal group named "Suggestions"; each is a button with a 48dp touch target.
While pending, "Sending…" is announced through a polite live region that is always present, and the field, Send and suggestions report disabled.
The "Ask AI" item is a regular item of the system selection menu, built with the same Foundation API as Cut, Copy and Paste; picking it closes the menu before onAskAi runs.
The Material 3 drag handle keeps its TalkBack collapse and dismiss actions, with a 48dp touch target reserved around it.
edgeCases: A blank prompt or blank suggestion is never sent; the prompt is trimmed before onSubmit.
Context longer than 140 characters is cut at a character boundary with trailing spaces removed and an ellipsis added; blank context shows no excerpt.
The toolbar may move "Ask AI" to its overflow menu when there is no room after Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all.
The TextFieldState overload adds nothing while only a caret is placed, so the caret menu (Paste) is unchanged.
Long prompts grow the field up to eight lines and then scroll inside it.

}

    MonarchButton(
        text = "Edit paragraph with AI",
        onClick = {},
        variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary,
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
    )
    MonarchAiInlinePrompt(
        onDismissRequest = {},
        onSubmit = {},
        context = "The team shipped the new onboarding flow in March. Early numbers suggest more people finish setup on their first visit, although the sample is still small and support tickets have not changed much yet.",
        suggestions = listOf("Shorten", "Make it more formal", "Fix spelling and grammar"),
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: The web opens a floating panel under the paragraph, with the keyboard shortcuts line (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line, Esc to close). On a phone the on-screen keyboard covers the area under a paragraph, so the same panel (the selection, the prompt field with Send and the three quick prompts, in the web's order) opens as a bottom sheet above the keyboard, and the keyboard shortcuts line is left out because a phone has no Shift+Enter or Esc.
parityExceptions.convention: Material bottom sheet for input that the keyboard would cover; no hardware-key hints on a touch device
